newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine debt buy-back may be in 1997 - official.
newsitem.headline: Argentine debt buy-back may be in 1997 - official.

text.p: Argentina could launch a debt buy-back in 1997 if it receives a suffiently attractive proposal, but none is yet imminent, Finance Undersecretary Miguel Kiguel said Monday.
"We don't think that the proposals we have so far are sufficiently attractive to go ahead with it now. If we have an attractive offer we are going to do it," Kiguel told reporters.
He added that current spreads between Argentine debt and U.S. Treasuries meant that Argentina is opting to issue debt for a seven-year term.
The government announced earlier Monday that it will shortly issue a seven-year $750-million global bond, to be placed by Credit Suisse First Boston and SBC Warburg.
In addition, Kiguel said that Argentina will issue another $1.7 billion in bonds on international markets and $750 million in bonds in Argentina during the rest of the year.
"Of those $750 million, $500 million will be obtained by expanding BONTES and $250 milion in a Letes tender in October," he said.
He added that Argentina will repay $10.0-10.5 billion in public debt in 1998.
